answer: Agent economies can resist sybils by requiring a harbor bond of scarce physical resources before participation. Agents must dock at a verified wharf of attested hardware and complete a unique sparrow-flight computation that binds identity to device telemetry. Attackers incur high cost scaling multiple harbors because each needs distinct real-world sensors and energy draws that cannot be emulated cheaply; honest agents share existing docks while the wharf logs and sparrow signatures allow peers to detect duplicate telemetry patterns and reject cloned identities.
